note: Config of tools/fwbudget.py. 'modules' attribute every byte of today's link (first matching rule wins; obj = object basename or lib:<archive>:<member>, sec = input-section name; 'as' overrides the memory class) and cap each module per class (irom / wram / wcode / brain; per variant when the cap is {test:{..}, release:{..}}). The linker's alignment fill is its own module, so the totals equal layout.txt's. Today's caps are the measured sizes (max of TEST and RELEASE): the 0.2.6 modules are frozen (milestone 1), so any growth is a deliberate change that must move its cap. 'plan' is the 0.3.0 module budget per placement. Each number says how it is known: measured (from a build) or estimated (calculated, with the basis given); the 'label' fields mark them MEASURED or MODELLED. Terms: s1 = the new 0.3.0 firmware's source set (fwbuild.json "s1", built with FW_S1) and s5 = its s5 variants (FW_S5, with the song engine). The fates and bases name the steps of the 0.3.0 work as stages: stage 1 = the scheduler, dispatcher, boot and watchdog of the s1 set; stage 2 = the sprite engine (core/sprite); stage 3 = the unpackers, the zoom (F4 / F5), the saves and MegaWire; stage 5 = the song engine (core/song). W1-W15 are the work items of docs/STAGE1_PLAN.md section 4.7. The D numbers (D02, D23, ...) name the differences between the 0.2.6 firmware and the cart's chip that our study of the cart listed.

plan.note: Allocation ("budget") per 0.3.0 module = the target the module must meet; the sum per placement must fit its room (the check fails otherwise). lo / cen / hi = the forecast (basis corrected to Thumb-1 after the first study): the Thumb-1 spans of the chip x ratios against Cortex-M0, or measured sizes of code that exists, or measured sizes of a draft (the song engine, the 88 audio config and the synth state: the song-engine draft, folded in after its review; the sprite engine, the sparse block->id index and the sprite state: the sprite-engine draft, folded in after its review). The verdict block checks the resident code (IROM + window + WRAM-ROM) against its room per forecast and variant; the room is net of the data allocated in wram_upper. Labels: see "ratio_labels" and each module's "label".

ratio_checks.song_engine_draft: Measured (the song-engine draft of 2026-10-10, made outside this tree): a struct-based C port of the song engine (chip 12,364 Thumb) links at 1.341 x the Thumb with -Os and 1.603 x with -O2. Against the ratios: R_OS 1.406 held (the port is 4.6 % smaller), R_O2 1.593 held (+0.6 %), R_PORT 1.12 is refuted for this module, and R_DEC (2.039 on AUD) overstated it: the compiled C of the chip's routines is 1.29 x (-Os) / 1.20 x (-O2) the draft on A1-A6, and on the audio posts that C glues the dispatcher fragments into much larger functions.
ratio_checks.gate_tables: Measured (the song-engine draft, audio commands): one 55-entry handler table serves both mailboxes (inferred for the entries not studied); gates as code: dispatcher entry + handler table 568 B -Os / 600 B -O2; table-driven gates: 1,100 / 1,212 B, and the audio handlers lose 332 / 400 B. Over the whole dispatcher a gate table saves about 0.45-0.57 KB (estimated from the audio rate), not ~3 KB. The dispatcher module keeps its forecast (it counts the chip's 662 B of dispatch tables; the draft needs 220 B) until the dispatcher itself is drafted.
ratio_checks.sprite_engine_draft: Measured (the sprite-engine draft of 2026-10-11, made outside this tree): a struct-based C port of the whole sprite engine links at 5,164 B -Os / 5,704 B -O2 against a forecast of 5,756 / 6,655 / 12,446. The chip's duplication disappears in a port (4,020 B of unrolled aging chains become a 164 B loop; three copies of search + claim become shared helpers; the per-mailbox dispatcher fragments become shared refusals). On the six routines the chip does not duplicate (1,826 Thumb) the port is 1.43 x (-Os) / 1.67 x (-O2) the Thumb, so R_OS 1.406 and R_O2 1.593 held within 2-5 %; R_DEC SPR 2.111 overstated the module because a Thumb x ratio basis cannot see the duplication (the compiled C of the chip's routines is 1.10 x / 1.03 x the draft on those six routines).

plan.ratio_basis: Cortex-M0 (Thumb-1): the cart program is Thumb-1 code (0 IT instructions; the only real 32-bit instructions are BL and ARMv6-M barriers; measured, and measured again). The earlier Cortex-M4 ratios (R_OS 1.508, R_O2 1.708, R_DEC 1.952) overstated the central forecast of every Thumb-based module by 7.3 %; the hi forecast (R_DEC) moves by under 1 % (the C of the chip's routines compiles to the same size for both cores, M0/M4 1.006).

ratio_labels.R_OS: Measured: same C (our 0.2.6 app sources) compiled RV32IM -Os and Cortex-M0 -Os, .text + .rodata
ratio_labels.R_DEC: PROXY: code written by our team from our own study of how the cart behaves, one function for each routine of the cart program (620 of 737 functions), compiled RV32IM -O2 and Cortex-M0 -Os, per subsystem; stands in for a straight port in the code style of the chip
ratio_labels.R_PORT: PROXY, inferred: our 0.2.6 sprite rows that do what the chip does, RV32 bytes per chip Thumb byte of the rows they cover; the row mapping is inferred
